headline: Tolle deals a gem as Red Sox survive Baltimore thriller
morning_brew: Tolle was absolute nails on the mound yesterday, going six strong innings and handing out twelve strikeouts like they were candy on Halloween. Getting that kind of performance in a tight race is exactly what we need, and seeing him shut down the Orioles while our offense did just enough to pull away was a beauty to behold. I been sayin' it all year, this team has the arms to compete if they just stay aggressive, and that was the most controlled I have seen our starter look in a long time.

The bullpen did their part too, with Miller, Morán, and Chapman closing the door without giving me a single cardiac event. We didn't need a huge offensive explosion to get the win, just a clean, professional game where everyone played their role to perfection. It is the kind of steady baseball that keeps the Duck Boat fund growing while we navigate this stretch run. My mother actually watched the whole thing without complaining once, which might be the most impressive stat of the entire night, considering she usually yells at the TV if the walk-up music is too loud.

We head into Sunday looking to keep this momentum rolling right through the weekend. The standings are tightening up, but for the first time in a while, I am feeling less like I am watching a car crash and more like I am watching a team that knows the stakes. We have eighteen games left in the regular season, and if we keep grinding out wins like this, we are going to be a tough out for anybody in the American League.
